result.summary: Enables clang-tidy performance checks for string handling: `performance-string-view-conversions`, `performance-prefer-single-char-overloads`, and `performance-faster-string-find`. It updates codebase call sites across multiple files to adhere to these rules, replacing multi-character string finds or conversions with single-character or string view equivalents.
result.problem: The codebase does not enforce clang-tidy string performance checks, allowing avoidable intermediate `std::string` allocations and suboptimal multi-character search overloads when operating on single characters.
evidence: PR description: 'E.g. on aarch64, when running the `BlockToJsonVerboseWrite` bench, I can see a minimal 0.3% drop in instructions and 0.6% drop in branches.'
result.scope_notes: Mechanical code cleanup across 21 files accompanied by enabling the corresponding clang-tidy linter checks.
result.card: Enables clang-tidy string performance rules (performance-string-view-conversions, performance-prefer-single-char-overloads, and performance-faster-string-find) and adjusts call sites across 21 files. It addresses micro-inefficiencies where string conversions or searches create unnecessary std::string copies or use multi-char overloads. The author measures a minor 0.3% drop in instructions and 0.6% drop in branches in the BlockToJsonVerboseWrite benchmark on aarch64. It has no dependencies.

risk.why: Mistakes in string find or conversion overloads could alter parsing or string manipulation behavior, but clang-tidy rules and unit tests constrain the scope to equivalent overloads.
